solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Analysis of matter I found in complex tracheotomy

indicators.note: the letter I is discovered sitting within the jumbled letters of the next word
complex means intricate or tangled, so the letters of tracheotomy are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have spotted something inside an intricate throat operation, as if examining the stuff of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' rearranges TRACHEOTOMY and 'found in' puts the I somewhere among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The theory that all matter is made of tiny indivisible particles is a scientific account of what substance consists of.

clue.text: Rides again to take in the Ring?

indicators.note: to take in means to enclose, so the word for again goes around the other piece

parts.note: bis is a musical direction meaning repeat, or again
Wagner's Ring is an opera cycle, the Ring cycle

explanation.surface: A rider goes round the circuit once more.
explanation.walkthrough: BIS, the musical instruction for a repeat, holds CYCLE; Wagner's four Ring operas are known as the Ring cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider sits on a two-wheeler, and as nouns rides can mean the machines themselves, in casual use.

clue.text: Nasty sweet, lacking honey

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the honey part is taken away

parts.note: sweet-sounding music is melodious
mel is Latin for honey, used in pharmacy

explanation.surface: A sugary sweet without honey tastes horrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' is sweet music, MELODIOUS, not confectionery; MEL, Latin for honey, comes off the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something unpleasant or hateful, a straightforward synonym pairing.

clue.text: Brewed tea's piping, encouraging consumption?

indicators.note: brewed suggests stewing and mixing, so the letters of the following words are reworked

explanation.surface: A steaming pot of freshly made tea makes one want to drink it.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's supplies a letter S here, as part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that whets the appetite tempts one to eat, which is a playful way of saying it encourages consumption.

clue.text: Last piece taken from side dish

indicators.note: the final letter is removed from the word for side

parts.note: the flank of something is its side

explanation.surface: Someone eating takes the final helping from a side dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side dish' looks like one phrase, but 'side' is FLANK and 'dish' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An open pastry case with a filling is a kind of tart served as a course.

clue.text: One reckoning to restrict central heating — it's a hot day

indicators.note: to restrict means to confine, so the scorer's word goes around the heating letters

parts.note: a scorer reckons up the points in a game
CH is the usual abbreviation for central heating in house adverts

explanation.surface: A meter reader keeps the radiators off because it is sweltering outside.
explanation.walkthrough: CH, the estate agents' abbreviation, sits inside SCORER.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially a blazing summer day with the sun beating down is called by this term.

clue.text: China about to go after one million antelopes

indicators.note: to go after means to follow, so these pieces come later in the answer

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
china is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate) for mate, so pal
a is an old short form meaning about or on, as in a-hunting

explanation.surface: Porcelain about to be shipped follows a single million-pound order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is rhyming slang: china plate = mate, so PAL.
explanation.definitionFit: This African animal is a type of antelope, and the word is used unchanged as its plural.

clue.text: I go after fiend chasing new soldiers

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the enthusiast comes after the new letter
after means coming later, so the attempt is placed at the end

parts.note: a fiend in the sense of an addict or enthusiast is a fan
to have a go is to make a try

explanation.surface: A demon is pursued by someone pressing on after a newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiend' is the enthusiast sense, as in a fitness fiend.
explanation.definitionFit: Foot soldiers collectively make up this branch of an army.

clue.text: Terror, taken on, lacking energy for musical interval

parts.note: T as a short form of terror

indicators.note: lacking means missing, so the energy letter is removed

parts.note: staff taken on are hired
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Fear, once accepted, leaves one drained of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: The interval spanning three notes of a diatonic scale, such as C to E, has this name.

clue.text: Brit seizing vermin, going to an officer

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the Brit's word goes around the vermin

parts.note: Pom is Australian slang for a Briton
lice are parasitic vermin

explanation.surface: An Englishman grabs a pest and hands it over to an official.
explanation.walkthrough: POM is Australian and New Zealand slang for a British person.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is an officer of the law, a member of the police force.

clue.text: Year's work recalled in chap's construction for spring festivity

indicators.note: in means inside, so these pieces sit within the chap's word

parts.note: a chap is a male
Y is the abbreviation for year

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word for work is read backwards

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A man looks back over a year's labour building something for May Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction' looks like part of the wordplay's container signal, but it belongs to the definition; the container signal is only 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall decorated pole is put up for villagers to dance around in traditional May celebrations.

clue.text: I take leading position in North America — a blissful state

indicators.note: in means inside, so these pieces sit within the continent's letters

parts.note: R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
the van, or vanguard, is the leading position

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of reaching the top in America and finding total happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: R, from Latin recipe, is the prescription abbreviation for take.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism the final release from desire and suffering is a state of perfect peace.

clue.text: Famous people releasing book; endless gossip about one of the stars?

indicators.note: releasing means letting go of, so the book letter is dropped

parts.note: celebs is short for celebrities

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened gossip goes around the one
endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: a tale is a piece of gossip
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Celebrities who stop publishing memoirs provoke endless gossip about one star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of the stars' looks like the definition, but 'one' gives I and the definition is 'of the stars'.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestial describes the heavens, so it means pertaining to the sky and its bodies.

clue.text: Source of watchmaker's humiliation?

parts.note: a watchmaker who mislays a dial would suffer this, and the phrase is also a term for public humiliation

explanation.surface: What could embarrass a watch craftsman?
explanation.walkthrough: A watch's dial is its face, so mislaying one is a literal version of the idiom for being disgraced.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a damaging blow to one's dignity, and a watch dial is literally its face.

clue.text: Try and try to lose railway's vital part

parts.note: to try a case in court is to hear it

indicators.note: to lose means to give up, so the railway letters are removed

parts.note: taken as an attempt, the word itself
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Someone keeps attempting to shed the railway's essential section.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Try' is the courtroom sense, to hear a case.
explanation.definitionFit: The essential or central part of something is called its core or crux, by figurative use of the organ.

clue.text: Call about gruesome tics, corrected — by such superficial treatment?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the call goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: to cry is to call out

indicators.note: corrected means put right, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shouts about ugly twitches being fixed by a beauty procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superficial' is fair for a treatment aimed at outward looks rather than health, and the question mark flags that wit.
explanation.definitionFit: Operations to improve appearance work on the surface of the body, hence a superficial treatment.

clue.text: Catches some overseas trips in stations?

parts.note: to cop is to catch, as in cop a fish
hops are short flights abroad

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a few holidays abroad at railway termini.
explanation.walkthrough: Cop shop is British slang for a police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Police stations are colloquially called by this slangy rhyming name in Britain.

clue.text: The Spanish king, chased by Harry's dog

indicators.note: chased by means followed by, so the harrying word comes next

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
K is the chess abbreviation for king
to harry someone is to hound them

explanation.surface: A Spanish king is pursued by Prince Harry's pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a prince's name, but it is the verb meaning to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian elkhound is a breed of spitz used for hunting large game.

clue.text: Arts subject is enthralling first couple of students — they support leading figures

parts.note: Eng Lit, English literature, shortened

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the word is wraps around the student letters
the first two letters of students are taken

explanation.surface: A literature course captures a couple of students who back the top people.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of rule by a select few back those at the top, the leading figures of society.

clue.text: Spirit of Shakespeare seen in line? On the contrary, a different kind of spirit

indicators.note: seen in would put the spirit inside the line, but the next words flip that
on the contrary reverses the containment, so the line goes inside the spirit

parts.note: Puck is the sprite in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean sprite appears in a line of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' says PUCK goes inside L, and 'On the contrary' swaps that, putting L inside PUCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage or spirit is called this, a different sense of spirit from a ghost or sprite.

clue.text: "United heading off supremacy": sport assessor

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, is taken off the word for supremacy

parts.note: empire means supreme rule or dominion

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline about a football team's dominance is judged by a sports pundit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the E from EMPIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The official who judges play in cricket or tennis decides on points of the game.

clue.text: Scientist's point about earth on record

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the point goes around the other pieces

parts.note: the gist is the main point
E is the electrical symbol for earth
o' is a short poetic form of on
a log is a record

explanation.surface: A researcher's main argument concerns the planet, put on file.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Scientist's' is a link meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist who studies rocks and the structure of the planet is a kind of scientist.

clue.text: Smith's antagonist decapitated horse with twisted rein

indicators.note: decapitated means having the head cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy horse

indicators.note: twisted means contorted, so the letters of rein are rearranged

explanation.surface: A beheaded horse with its bridle tangled is someone's enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: In Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four, Winston Smith is tortured by the Party official of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four pits Winston Smith against this Inner Party interrogator.

clue.text: See 1
Heroin? I lead individual to get part of joint

parts.note: H is slang for heroin
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A drug user asks about leading someone to a share of a cannabis joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' is the metal, symbol PB, not to guide; 'joint' is the hip, not a reefer.
explanation.definitionFit: The bone forming the socket of the hip is part of that ball-and-socket joint.

clue.text: Leave, having abandoned computer technology?

parts.note: ex describes something given up, a former thing
IT stands for information technology

explanation.surface: Someone quits after giving up working in computing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'having abandoned computer technology' as ex-IT, someone formerly in IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To go out of a place or depart is a plain synonym for leave, as a verb.

clue.text: Concern after losing a hat likely to grow a good deal

definitions.text: likely to grow a good deal

indicators.note: after losing means once it has gone without, so the letter a is taken away

parts.note: fear is anxiety or concern
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: An anxious person loses a hat that seemed bound to get bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: TILE is dated British slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich soil or a productive mind yields abundantly, so it is apt to produce plenty.

clue.text: Airborne soldier: no account involving one showing cracks?

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A paratrooper has no record of anyone showing structural weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracks' plays on cracked, slang for mentally unhinged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with deep irrational suspicion is said, informally, to be cracked, hence showing cracks.

clue.text: Go in for chips but not fish

indicators.note: but not means except for, so the fish is removed

parts.note: Chips is the traditional nickname for a ship's carpenter
a carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone opts for chips and not fish at the chippy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chips but not fish' suggests a takeaway order; Chips is the old naval nickname for a ship's carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: To come or go into a place is a plain synonym, a verb matching the phrase.
